responsibility: Contains the main implementation of the Xtensa GCC backend outside the declarative machine description. It owns target hooks and helper routines for option override, register usage, addressing legitimacy, constant pools and literal placement, cost modeling, calling convention and varargs, builtins, TLS and trampolines, prologue/epilogue and frame layout, block move and atomic expansion, branch/call emission, MI thunks, and the machine-dependent reorg pass for Xtensa hardware loop optimization, translating generic GCC RTL/tree operations into Xtensa-specific code-generation behavior.
same_name_distinction: Among the xtensa.* files, this is the imperative C++ backend implementation: it defines target hooks, expansion/helpers, and the machine-dependent reorg pass, while xtensa.h provides macro/ABI definitions, xtensa.md provides declarative RTL patterns and scheduling, and xtensa.opt defines command-line options and target variables.
